title: T1001.002 — Data Obfuscation - Steganography
subtitle: Watch a payload smuggle itself in, and see which signals the defenders can catch.

nodes.label: Sensitive data
nodes.tip: Sensitive data - What is at risk

steps.title: Load the cover page
steps.caption: chip:'Browse' Load the cover page. The user opens a blog page on gallery.example. The page itself is clean; nothing malicious is downloaded yet
steps.defender: plain browsing, nothing to alert on yet - this is the baseline.

steps.title: Download the carrier image
steps.caption: chip:'Fetch PNG' Download the carrier image. The browser fetches banner.png, about 1.2 MB. The picture is served only to this organization, so its hash will look unique and unknown
steps.defender: a full-size PNG from a small, rare image host - note the size and the host.

steps.title: Read the hidden data
steps.caption: chip:'Extract' Read the hidden data. The implant on the workstation opens the PNG as a file and reads the embedded bytes. The picture is never executed - it is only read, which is why the file itself stays clean
steps.defender: Sysmon EID15 logs the stream hash of the image file.

steps.title: Start the extracted stage
steps.caption: chip:'Run' Start the extracted stage. The extracted code runs in memory through rundll32.exe. No new file of its own is written, so file-based tools see little
steps.defender: process lineage shows rundll32 with an image-file event right before it.

steps.title: Upload data inside a screenshot
steps.caption: chip:'Stego exfil' Upload data inside a screenshot. The implant takes a screenshot, hides collected data in it, and POSTs shot.png back to the image host. It looks like a normal image upload
steps.defender: a 640 KB image POST - the first image upload this workstation has ever made.

steps.title: Content checks pass
steps.caption: chip:'Hash miss' Content checks pass. Antivirus and DLP inspect the upload. It is a structurally valid PNG with an unknown hash, so the verdict is clean
steps.defender: AV/DLP verdict clean - this is the blind spot of content-only review.

steps.title: Analytics catch the pattern
steps.caption: chip:'Workflow alert' Analytics catch the pattern. A workflow rule fires: first-ever image POST from 10.2.4.15, to an image host registered nine days ago
steps.defender: workflow beats content - rarity and lineage, not the picture itself, raise the alert.

detection.label: Alert raised
detection.detail: The SOC has enough evidence to open an incident.

steps.title: Contain and investigate
steps.caption: chip:'Respond' Contain and investigate. The SOC blocks the image host at the firewall, isolates the workstation, and keeps the PNG as evidence. Analysts confirm the hidden data with stego tools in the lab, on their own copy
steps.defender: quick containment, then careful lab analysis - never on production systems.
